I actually recently watched this too and the things that stood out as an anime to me were:

The art style. It seemed kind of trashy at first, but it was DIFFERENT, and the colors seem pretty skewed towards pastels instead of brighter colors. This was initially a turn off, but I grew to like it the more I watched it

The story's perspective. The story occasionally changed perspective to show events in time from different characters, not all the characters at the same time, but sometimes just from a different point of view (specifically i believe EP 4 was great because it was completely different from what you were expecting).

Unexpected ending. It defies the western direction shows take in order for the "feel good" ending and instead take a different, more interesting/realistic route. The final ending seems lack luster, but makes sense in the logical scheme of the world/lore.

40 Minutes episodes. This is unusual for anime, but typical for TV series with deep plot/lore to them. This gives enough time for each episode to ramp up, peak, and wind down and wrap its own episode plot up and still leave time for a main overarching plot. Additionally leaves time for more traditional drama styles.
